items.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I did work at Nick’s for a while, Nick’s with Phil Napoleon... I was at Nick’s with Phil Napoleon in ’54... I got a call from Phil Napoleon again... I had never worked directly for Gleason, but worked for Phil, Phil Napoleon.

ctx.x: Yeah. That whole scene, that as you said Condonites, what was it that made that almost a style in itself, the way those guys played or just their personalities?

Well the informality of it was very important. It was loose and relaxed. Well I’m going ahead of myself, but I’m going way ahead of myself, I don’t know how far do you want me to go on this thing. But I did work at Nick’s for a while, Nick’s with Phil Napoleon and later on with Pee Wee Irwin. And this is in the 50s, the mid-50s. And Nick’s was a very formal place. The music was very strict and they wanted you to play a certain style, two beat more or less, and don’t swing too much. Yeah, yeah really. I mean the…
Well I hear, I mean I’ve read of course that he was a major league drinker.
